teachingNotesSuggested.note: Use 둘/셋/넷 when counting alone, and 두/세/네 before counters: 두 명, 세 권, 네 개.
당신 is context-sensitive; in everyday conversation a person's name/title or an omitted pronoun is often more natural.
Floor numbers use the Japanese convention: the ground entrance level is floor 1. Do not assess the English/British versus Japanese numbering convention without this context.
半 means half. Time example: 二時半（にじはん）= 2:30; Indonesian setengah tiga also means 2:30.
必ず means an event/action occurs without fail. Contrast もちろん, conversational of course.
In the taught かね reading use money. The ordinary gold noun is read きん. Bare written 金 needs a reading or context.
やめる is quitting/stopping an activity. とめる is stopping movement, as in a car. Written spelling alone is insufficient for a listening question.
少ない = not many/not much; 少し = a few/a little. These should not be treated as interchangeable quantities.

Generic Japanese ～つ counters can count concrete objects or abstract matters. Existing other-language count glosses select abstract things in several rows; use object context when testing counters instead of claiming a universal one-to-one noun mapping.
Existing valid sentences mix polite endings and plain/casual endings. Teach the register explicitly rather than presenting every sentence as interchangeable in all social situations.
Thai ฉัน and Vietnamese tôi/bạn are useful learner defaults but pronouns and polite particles depend on speaker, relationship and setting.

audioIntegrationRisks: current-form-pronunciation.js validates 5,906 baseline forms against normalized text before it registers aliases; load reviewed corrections after that baseline, or deliberately update validation. Do not edit a baseline wording and leave the assertion invalid.

native-pronunciation.js resolves an alias from the normalized exact current text, which is a suitable stale-audio safeguard when new forms have no clip. Do not add semantic-ID aliases pointing new text at old recordings.
Review changed language/text/gender combinations for exact existing recording matches, otherwise show honest unavailable/device-voice fallback. No paid regeneration is authorized.
Written Japanese homographs such as 金/日/月/後/止める need reading-aware listening selection. This review did not listen to the bundled clips, so their actual homograph pronunciation is not certified.
limitations: Text review covers all assigned 8,040 multilingual forms and all 1,000 Japanese native triples, not every generated runtime question, answer variant, grammar explanation, or audio clip.
No physical Android test, live account, progress mutation, purchase, deployment or publication was performed.
Valid dialect, politeness and synonym alternatives were retained where the supplied context does not select a single form.
Native-speaker editorial review and end-to-end pronunciation audition remain independent quality checks; this report does not certify native-level accuracy.

unresolvedIssues.action: Root should add contextual teaching notes and avoid claiming universal equivalence for pronouns, honorifics, suffixes and polysemous standalone kanji.

Root should ensure corrected forms appear in new questions and refreshed saved review cards, exact text audio never points at obsolete wording, and duplicate synonym choices cannot yield arbitrary scoring.
